messages.subject: buildtemplate coding problem
parts:
Hi, 

I am new to the geomorph package and am having trouble with the buildtemplate function. I am trying to use the geomorph package to analyze the shape characteristics of the calcanei (heel foot bones) of different foot types. I have been able to read in a ".ply" file that contains a 3d mesh of the bone as well as a matrix of landmark points that I have selected externally. My issue has been with the repeatability of the build template function when I ask the function to select 200 more surface semilandmarks. When I read in the same file with the same landmark points and ask the function to create the surface semilandmarks, the build template function gives me a different series of semilandmarks each time. I am not sure if this is an inherent property of the function causing some variability with the semilandmark points, or if I am using the function incorrectly. I have been able to use the template built from this function effectively in the digitize surface function and have done some Principal component analysis with results that are similar but not identical when using the same data. Additionally, I am not attempting to use the curve sliders, just the surface semilandmarks for this case. Any help on the buildtemplate function or further explanation would be great. I am currently calling the function as follows,

buildtemplate(get(bone_surface_name),get(bone_landmark_name),200, ptsize=0.5, center=TRUE)

where I had previously assigned the variables "bone_surface_name" and "bone_landmark_name" to their respective ".ply" and matrix files using the read.ply and as.matrix functions. 

Thanks, 
Erik

I have checked this and confirm your observation: 

lmk <- as.matrix(read.csv("app01_Right_calcaneuslandmarks.csv", sep=" ", header=F))
ply <- read.ply("app01_Right_calcaneus.ply")

temp1 <- buildtemplate(ply, lmk, 200, center = F)
temp2 <- buildtemplate(ply, lmk, 200, center = F)
temp3 <- buildtemplate(ply, lmk, 200, center = F)

shade3d(ply, col="grey")
points3d(lmk, col="red", size=10)
points3d(temp1, col="blue", size=10)
points3d(temp2, col="green", size=10)
points3d(temp3, col="black", size=10)

























I have also checked with a few other datasets and found the same. There I must apologise but my original comment was incorrect, no the templates will not always be the same. As I re-familiarise myself with the function (which I worked on a long while ago), I see now that in a 3D case, with such a large point cloud, and only 100 iterations allowed, the function kmeans will always find a slightly different result. But the results are never very different.

Hi Emma, 

Would you mind taking a quick look at my R code and let me know if you see any obvious errors, perhaps in the way I am reading in the data or calling it in the gpagen, digitsurface, or any where else. As before, I am trying to quantify shape differences in foot bones using the geomorph GPA and Principal component analysis. I have included my code for the talus, which is the same as the calcaneus (the example specimen from prior posts), as well as another .csv and .ply file for my input and the correspond .nts file that is output. The sizes of the point cloud and landmarks is similar for all the bones of the talus's and calcaneus's. I have roughly 40 separate specimen for each bone type and am running into an issue when performing my principal component analysis using the generalized procrustes aligned landmarks/semilandmarks. More often than not, when I run the PCA, the analysis results have been variable enough to the point where the same exact landmarks and surfaces will give different statistically significant principal components. I am also noticing that it takes nearly 20 Principal components to account for ~90% of the variation (out of 40 PC's), and the variance even from the first few components does not add up as quickly as other examples. I am wondering if there is a reason as to why it is taking this many Principal components to describe the variation, or if that is the nature of these foot bones. Thanks for any help provided.

Erik

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: buildtemplate coding problem
parts:
Dear Erik,

I've looked over your code, and I don't see an obvious errors. 

With large datasets of semilandmarks, it is quite common to have many PCs accounting for the variation. Landmark data in general also. It's what people shifting from linear measurement data often notice.

What I suspect might be happening with the variability is this: So we established that the kmeans method of making the template isn't producing the exact same solution every time. Plus, the TPS warping for fitting the template to the other surfaces is done using only the 10 fixed lmks, and will "snap" to the points on the mesh. I see that the mesh has a very rough surface, due to the scan resolution being very low, which means it could be enough to create very big differences between different template iterations. None of these methods are perfect, and there may be samples where it doesn't work as well as others. I think the low resolution of these scans is certainly adding unnecessary "shape differences", which are being picked up by the very subtle changes that 200 semis are covering.

Hope that helps

Emma
